neighbours.label: A list, not yet a pattern: the second piece of a few specific two-part names — ' George' after 'Lake', ' grain' after 'long', 'at/ats' after 'J' or 'Lands' (Jats, Landsat). The same tokens elsewhere ('George Washington', 'a grain of sand') and other lakes stay quiet.
fire: Our cabin was a short walk from Lake George, where we swam every morning.
For a fluffy pilaf you should rinse the long grain rice three times.
Many farmers in Haryana are Jats who have worked the same land for centuries.
The researchers compared Landsat pictures taken ten years apart.
A ferry crosses Lake George twice a day during the summer months.
The shop sells brown rice, wild rice and long grain varieties in bulk.
In the villages around Delhi the Jats hold most of the farmland.
Forest loss in the region was mapped with Landsat data from 1990 onward.
quiet: Our cabin was a short walk from Lake Tahoe, where we swam every morning.
For a fluffy pilaf you should rinse the basmati rice three times.
Many farmers in Haryana are Sikhs who have worked the same land for centuries.
The researchers compared satellite pictures taken ten years apart.
A statue of King George stands in the square beside the old town hall.
The shop sells every grain you can think of, from barley to millet, in bulk.
Her uncle George drove the ferry twice a day during the summer months.
The table was sanded with the grain and finished with two coats of oil.

notes: Weak pole (max 5.84). Probes: 'Lake George' 0.86, 'long grain' 0.88, 'Landsat' 0.56, 'Jats' 0.48; 'George Washington' 0.003, 'grain of sand' 0.004, 'wood grain' 0.008, 'Lake Tahoe' 0.06, 'Lawton' 0.17. Many first parts begin with L or J (Lake, long, Lands, Law, lat, J), which may be the real link; I could not find the shared pattern, so only the list is claimed.
